About the Position

Focusing on the biomechanics of hip replacement surgery and peri-prosthetic fracture, this PhD is part of the EPSRC Faculty with Industry DTP Award 2026/27.

OpportunityFully Funded PhD Studentship Biomechanics of Hip Replacement Surgery and Peri-Prosthetic Fracture
HostUniversity of Leeds
LocationLeeds, United Kingdom
Study LevelPhD
FundingFully Funded
Stipend£21,805 per year (tax-free)
Application Deadline30 September 2026 at 05:00 UTC+5
ApplyOfficial application page ↗

Basic Information

  • Project Title: PhD Opportunity in Biomechanics of Hip Replacement Surgery and Peri-Prosthetic Fracture
  • Host Institution: University of Leeds
  • School/Faculty: Faculty of Engineering and Physical Sciences (Mechanical Engineering)
  • Disciplines: Mechanical Engineering, Medicine, Biomechanics
  • Study Level: PhD
  • Application Deadline: 30 September 2026 at 05:00 UTC+5
  • Funding Type: Fully Funded (EPSRC)
  • Eligibility: UK Only
  • Location: Leeds, United Kingdom
  • IELTS Required: Yes

Research Position Overview

This opportunity is part of the EPSRC Faculty with Industry Doctoral Training Partnership Award 2026/27. It focuses on the biomechanics of hip replacement surgery and peri-prosthetic fracture, offering a collaborative environment with industry partners. University of Leeds is seeking candidates for this PhD opportunity focused on PhD Studentship Biomechanics of Hip Replacement Surgery and Peri-Prosthetic Fracture. The work sits within Mechanical Engineering, Medicine, Biomechanics. Location: Leeds, United Kingdom. According to the listing, funding covers the full cost of participation; financial support is listed as £21,805 per year (tax-free). Applications close 30 September 2026 at 05:00 UTC+5.

Research Context

Hip replacements are common, but peri-prosthetic fractures remain a serious complication. Understanding the biomechanical factors can improve implant design and surgical outcomes.

What You Will Do

You will conduct experimental and/or computational biomechanics research, working closely with industrial collaborators to address real-world challenges.

Key Research Aims

  • Investigate the mechanical behaviour of hip implants and surrounding bone.
  • Identify risk factors for peri-prosthetic fractures.
  • Develop strategies to improve implant longevity and patient safety.

Supervisor Profile

Supervisor details are not listed. Please refer to the School of Mechanical Engineering website at Leeds for potential supervisors.

Eligibility and Requirements

  • Academic Background: First-class or 2:1 Honours degree (or equivalent) in mechanical engineering, biomedical engineering, or a related discipline.
  • English Language: IELTS required.
  • Nationality: UK only.

Funding Details

  • Funding Type: EPSRC Doctoral Training Partnership (DTP) studentship.
  • Stipend: £21,805 per year (tax-free).
  • Duration: 3.5 years.
  • Fees: Full academic fees covered.

How to Apply

Apply online via the University of Leeds PhD application portal.

Official Link

https://phd.leeds.ac.uk/project/2526-phd-opportunity-in-biomechanics-of-hip-replacement-surgery-and-peri-prosthetic-fracture

Important Notes

  • Always confirm the full requirements and current deadline on the official website before applying.
  • Prepare the requested documents early — competitive awards are often decided on complete, on-time submissions.
  • Funding terms shown here reflect the listing at the time of publication and can be updated by the provider.
